350: pub fn covered_bare_rewrite(
351:     rewritten: &RoaringBitmap,
352:     indices: &[IndexMetadata],
353: ) -> Option<BareRewriteRefusal> {
354:     indices
355:         .iter()
356:         .filter(|index| index.name != MEM_WAL_INDEX_NAME)
357:         .find_map(|index| match index.fragment_bitmap.as_ref() {
358:             Some(bitmap) if bitmap.is_disjoint(rewritten) => None,
359:             Some(bitmap) => Some(BareRewriteRefusal::Covered {
360:                 index: index.name.clone(),
361:                 overlap: bitmap & rewritten,
362:             }),
363:             None => Some(BareRewriteRefusal::UnknownCoverage {
364:                 index: index.name.clone(),
365:             }),
366:         })
367: }

1510: /// Assemble the tagged FRI entry a rewrite commits, and return it with the
1511: /// `dataset_version` of the entry it appended onto.
1512: ///
1513: /// `transitions` are the records the rewrite adds (what its
1514: /// `frag_reuse_index` holds beyond the entry at its read version, see
1515: /// `records_added_since`). The current entry's content bytes are carried
1516: /// over verbatim (a v0 entry is lifted to index_version 1 by
1517: /// reinterpretation, not re-encoding) and each new transition is appended as
1518: /// another `InlineContent.transitions` element. Before anything is spilled
1519: /// or committed, the binding between the rewrite groups and the transitions
1520: /// is validated (sources and destinations must match the groups' old and new
1521: /// fragments one to one, in order), row counts must be conserved, no added
1522: /// transition may already be recorded, and the whole assembled content must
1523: /// decode as a valid ledger.
1524: pub(crate) async fn build_frag_reuse_rewrite_entry(
1525:     dataset: &Dataset,
1526:     transitions: &[pb_fri::Transition],
1527:     groups: &[RewriteGroup],
1528: ) -> lance_core::Result<(IndexMetadata, Option<u64>)> {
1529:     // The spec excludes tagged histories on stable-row-id tables: the FRI is
1530:     // address-based, and under stable row ids a rewrite's rows keep their
1531:     // ids, so there is no address translation to record. The planner blocks
1532:     // the deferred-compaction combination already; this covers a hand-built
1533:     // rewrite committed directly.
1534:     if dataset.manifest.uses_stable_row_ids() {
1535:         return Err(Error::not_supported(
1536:             "Tagged fragment reuse histories are address-based and excluded on \
1537:              stable-row-id datasets; this rewrite cannot carry transition intent here",
1538:         ));
1539:     }
1540: 
1541:     if transitions.is_empty() {
1542:         return Err(Error::invalid_input(
1543:             "a fragment-reuse rewrite carries no transitions",
1544:         ));
1545:     }

668:     /// Remap the row ids, creating a new remapped version of this index in `dest_store`
669:     ///
670:     /// Legacy remapping API using an in-memory mapping. Retained for existing
671:     /// callers and plugins; new tagged fragment reuse maintenance goes through
672:     /// [`Self::remap_streaming`], whose default implementation prepares a
673:     /// complete in-memory mapping and calls this method once.
674:     async fn remap(
675:         &self,
676:         mapping: &RowAddrRemap,
677:         dest_store: &dyn IndexStore,
678:     ) -> Result<CreatedIndex>;
679: 
680:     /// The fragments whose row addresses this index's files may hold, or
681:     /// `None` when the index cannot tell.
682:     ///
683:     /// Only the in-memory fallback of [`Self::remap_streaming`] reads it: an
684:     /// address left out of the mapping it prepares stays unchanged through
685:     /// [`Self::remap`], so the fallback maps every address of every listed
686:     /// fragment explicitly, and declines when the list is unknown. An
687:     /// implementation that overrides this must list every fragment its files
688:     /// can hold addresses for, including fragments the index no longer claims
689:     /// in its declared coverage (a retired source, or one withdrawn after an
690:     /// in-place rewrite). Not needed by indices that implement
691:     /// `remap_streaming` themselves.
692:     fn stored_fragments(&self) -> Option<RoaringBitmap> {
693:         None
694:     }
695: 
696:     /// Remap the row ids through a translator whose payload may need reads,
697:     /// creating a new remapped version of this index in `dest_store`.
698:     ///
699:     /// The default implementation keeps existing indices working: a
700:     /// synchronous translator is handed to [`Self::remap`] as it is, and a
701:     /// batch translator is first materialized into a complete in-memory
702:     /// mapping ([`materialize_remap`], bounded by the translator's budget and
703:     /// requiring [`Self::stored_fragments`]) before one call to
704:     /// [`Self::remap`]. That fallback costs the mapping's memory and reads the
705:     /// index once more; it declines with a
706:     /// [`RemapUnavailable`](crate::remapping::RemapUnavailable) it cannot
707:     /// prove a complete mapping within budget. Built-in indices override this
708:     /// to translate one unit of work at a time (a page, a partition, a spill
709:     /// batch) without any map sized to the source rows.
710:     async fn remap_streaming(
711:         &self,
712:         translator: &RowAddrTranslator,
713:         dest_store: &dyn IndexStore,
714:     ) -> Result<CreatedIndex> {
715:         match translator {
716:             RowAddrTranslator::Sync(mapping) => self.remap(mapping.as_ref(), dest_store).await,
717:             RowAddrTranslator::Batch(remapper) => {
718:                 let mapping =
719:                     materialize_remap(remapper.as_ref(), self.stored_fragments().as_ref()).await?;
720:                 self.remap(&mapping, dest_store).await
721:             }
722:         }
723:     }

865: async fn remap_index_tagged(dataset: &mut Dataset, index_id: &Uuid) -> Result<()> {
866:     // Stored metadata: the segment's provenance bitmap and the entry, never
867:     // the query-rewritten listing `load_indices` produces on tagged tables.
868:     let stored = read_manifest_indexes(
869:         &dataset.object_store,
870:         &dataset.manifest_location,
871:         &dataset.manifest,
872:     )
873:     .await?;
874:     let entry = stored
875:         .iter()
876:         .find(|idx| idx.name == FRAG_REUSE_INDEX_NAME)
877:         .ok_or_else(|| {
878:             Error::index("the fragment reuse index entry disappeared during remap".to_string())
879:         })?;
880:     let ledger = decode_frag_reuse_ledger(dataset, entry).await?;
881:     if ledger.has_unsupported_transitions() {
882:         return Err(Error::not_supported(
883:             "the tagged FRI history carries transitions this client cannot interpret; \
884:              upgrade to a newer version of Lance before remapping",
885:         ));
886:     }
887:     let curr_index_meta = stored
888:         .iter()
889:         .find(|idx| idx.uuid == *index_id)
890:         .cloned()
891:         .ok_or_else(|| {
892:             Error::index(format!(
893:                 "index {index_id} not found in manifest; it may have been concurrently dropped"
894:             ))
895:         })?;
896:     // Eligibility is decided at the plan level, before any file is read: a
897:     // segment the reader derives no coverage for is skipped when it will be
898:     // replaced anyway (withdrawn, superseded) or cannot be translated by
899:     // this build (nothing to restamp), and refused when its metadata cannot
900:     // be interpreted. A remap never publishes a bitmap for rows it did not
901:     // translate.
902:     match crate::index::frag_reuse::segment_coverage_reason(dataset, &curr_index_meta).await? {
903:         None => {}
904:         Some(
905:             reason @ (MissingCoverageReason::Withdrawn
906:             | MissingCoverageReason::NoDerivedCoverage
907:             | MissingCoverageReason::Unsupported),
908:         ) => {
909:             log::info!(
910:                 "Skipping remap of index {} ({}): {reason}. A rebuild (optimize) replaces it; \
911:                  queries are unaffected",
912:                 curr_index_meta.name,
913:                 curr_index_meta.uuid
914:             );
915:             return Ok(());
916:         }
917:         Some(MissingCoverageReason::Corrupt) => {
918:             return Err(Error::index(format!(
919:                 "index {} ({}) has metadata this build cannot interpret; rebuild the index",
920:                 curr_index_meta.name, curr_index_meta.uuid
921:             )));
922:         }
923:     }
924:     let Some(stored_bitmap) = curr_index_meta.fragment_bitmap.clone() else {
925:         log::warn!(
926:             "Index {} ({}) has no stored fragment bitmap; its lineage through the tagged \
927:              history cannot be determined, skipping remap. Consider rebuilding the index",
928:             curr_index_meta.name,
929:             curr_index_meta.uuid
930:         );
931:         return Ok(());
932:     };
933:     // A segment that predates a lifted v0 deferred compaction still holds
934:     // the group's source addresses behind a bitmap v0 swapped to the
935:     // destinations; plan from the fragments the file really addresses.
936:     let provenance = effective_provenance(&ledger, &stored_bitmap, curr_index_meta.dataset_version);
937: 
938:     let lineage = entry.fragment_bitmap.clone().unwrap_or_default();
939:     let (hops, mut coverage, admitted) = match plan_tagged_remap(
940:         &ledger,
941:         &provenance,
942:         dataset.fragment_bitmap.as_ref(),
943:         &lineage,
944:     ) {
945:         TaggedRemapPlan::Identity => return Ok(()),
946:         TaggedRemapPlan::Blocked { fragment } => {
947:             log::info!(
948:                 "Skipping remap of index {} ({}): at fragment {} its coverage reaches a \
949:                  transition it only partially covers (a stable partition, or any hop after \
950:                  a stable-partition restamp) or a retired fragment the history no longer \
951:                  maps. Queries keep translating through the reuse index; rebuild the index \
952:                  to catch it up",
953:                 curr_index_meta.name,
954:                 curr_index_meta.uuid,
955:                 fragment
956:             );
957:             return Ok(());
958:         }
959:         TaggedRemapPlan::Remap {
960:             hops,
961:             coverage,
962:             admitted,
963:         } => (hops, coverage, admitted),
964:     };
965: 
966:     if !hops.is_empty() {
967:         // The rewrite streams the segment through the reader's loading path,
968:         // and for index types that materialize their state at load (e.g.
969:         // bitmap) that path applies direct-coverage-wins: rows whose
970:         // translated destination is directly covered by a sibling segment
971:         // are ceded to it and absent from the loaded state. Publish only the
972:         // coverage the reader attributes to this segment, so the swapped
973:         // bitmap never claims rows the remapped file may not contain -- an
974:         // over-claim would later let segment pruning remove the sibling that
975:         // actually holds those rows. (For types that stream raw pages, e.g.
976:         // BTree, the rows the reader cedes are dropped by the translator's
977:         // claim filter below, so file and bitmap agree.)
978:         use crate::index::DatasetIndexExt;
979:         if let Some(listed) = dataset
980:             .load_indices()
981:             .await?
982:             .iter()
983:             .find(|idx| idx.uuid == *index_id)
984:             && let Some(servable) = &listed.fragment_bitmap
985:         {
986:             coverage &= servable;
987:         }
988:     }
989: 
990:     // Overlays committed after the source index was built are not
991:     // incorporated by the remap; exclude those fragments so queries scan
992:     // their current values instead (mirrors the v0 path).
993:     for fragment in dataset.manifest.fragments.iter() {
994:         let has_newer_indexed_overlay = fragment.overlays.iter().any(|overlay| {
995:             overlay.committed_version > curr_index_meta.dataset_version
996:                 && overlay
997:                     .data_file
998:                     .fields
999:                     .iter()
1000:                     .any(|field_id| curr_index_meta.fields.contains(field_id))
1001:         });
1002:         if has_newer_indexed_overlay {
1003:             coverage.remove(fragment.id as u32);
1004:         }
1005:     }
